Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015). ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch. The 18.0 QA sweep found this at 5b14b7f3 (or the hotcrm next.5 bump). Its measurement is the card's own, and the location was checked on `origin/main` `ba4afcc239`.

- **p2.** The public form leaves a required select empty where the option list marks `default: true`. So an anonymous visitor is refused "Required: Priority" on the client, while the server would accept and default the same submit. The visitor can still pick a value. It predates the bump (next.3 and next.5 both measured).
- **Lane `domain:ui`:** the public form renderer, in the same family as #11914 (the internal form). Fix it with the same rule the internal New form uses.
- **Not a protocol change:** a renderer applying a declared default.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `052b82360b0ee0b0ff74f7ebfb9571b271072df6`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #13049 (body, triage, claim, os-dev-report), PR #13058 (body, 7-file list, net diff against `main` at the head), the head's 35 check-runs, and the published source the diff touches on the local checkout (`packages/plugin-form/src/schemaDefaults.ts`, `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx`, `.changeset/config.json`, `scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `scripts/check-changeset-fixed.mjs`, AGENTS.md) plus the server's `ObjectQL.resolveOptionDefault` / `applyFieldDefaults` / `declaredMultiValued` in `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`. Nothing built, run or re-run.

Check-runs on the head at review time: completed `success` — Changeset Declaration, Changeset Claim Re-read, Changeset Fixed Group Check, Changeset Bump Policy, Changeset Overwrite Report, Line Citation Gate, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Bundle Analysis, label; `skipped` — Test (coverage), Test (coverage shard), dependabot; **still `in_progress`** — Type Check, Lint, Repo Gates, Build & E2E, Build Docs, Test (dist pins), Test shards 1/16 to 16/16, Live E2E (informational). No check-run has concluded `failure`. The derived-gate families (type-check, lint, vitest, build) are therefore not yet answered by CI; this record's verdict is the contract judgment and is not a substitute for those conclusions.

### ① Derived judgments

**Public-surface changes — exactly the two claimed, and the pin and README both say so. Right.**
- `packages/plugin-form/src/index.tsx` adds one runtime name, `optionListDefault` (re-exported from `./schemaDefaults`), and one type-only name, `OptionListFieldLike`. No other export line moves; `schemaDefaultValues`, `seedCreateValues`, `isSeedableDefault`, `isCreateFormMode` and `isRuntimeDefault` stay in the pin's `WITHHELD` list and off the entry.
- `entrySurface-6059.test.tsx`: `PUBLISHED` becomes the three names, the identity check (entry value `===` module value) still runs over all of them, and the "exactly those names and no others from this module" assertion is kept as a set comparison, so a fourth name from `schemaDefaults.ts` would still fail the pin. A new leg annotates with `OptionListFieldLike` (tsc judges the type export) and asserts no runtime key of that name.
- `README.md`: the entry import list gains `optionListDefault`, and one paragraph under "What a create form opens with" names the function, its parameter type, its consumer and the caller-owned `defaultValue` gate.
- One signature widening that is also published surface: the parameter goes from `SeedFieldLike | undefined` to `OptionListFieldLike | null | undefined`. Additive (a `null` is now accepted and answers `undefined` through the existing `field?.options` read). Right.

**`OptionListFieldLike` under objectui#7324 — the right shape. Right.**
- Members are `type`, `multiple`, `options`, all `unknown` — exactly the three keys the function body reads (`field?.options`, `field?.type`, `field?.multiple`) and nothing else. Not wider than what is read; not a widening of `FieldDefaultsSchemaLike` (whose member set the 7324 pin holds fixed).
- Every value the internal `SeedFieldLike` accepted still type-checks: `SeedFieldLike` is `{ defaultValue?, type?, reference? } & { options?, multiple? }`, which is structurally assignable to an all-optional, all-`unknown` interface, and the only internal call site (`schemaDefaultValues` passing the variable `f`) is not a fresh object literal, so no excess-property check applies. `f.meta` on the console side is `ObjectFieldDef | undefined`, assignable on the same grounds.

**Behaviour for `schemaDefaultValues`' existing callers — unchanged. Right.** The function body is byte-identical in the diff (only the signature line and the docblock change); `schemaDefaultValues` still reaches it through the same `dv == null` branch.

**`FormPage.readPrefill` precedence — matches the create form, and matches the server. Right.**
- Literal `defaultValue` wins: `f.defaultValue == null` is false for any literal (including `''`), so `fromOptions` is `undefined` and the pre-existing `else if` seeds the literal. The server's `applyFieldDefaults` uses the identical presence test (`if (f.defaultValue == null)` before `resolveOptionDefault`), so `''` wins over the flag on both sides.
- Runtime `defaultValue` is never replaced: a CEL envelope or token is not `== null`, so the flag is never consulted, and `isRuntimeDefault` keeps the key absent as before.
- `prefill_FIELD` wins: the query read is still the last write in the loop, after both default sources and after the record.
- Multi-valued fields seed an array: arity is decided inside `optionListDefault` via `isMultiValueField({ type, multiple })`, the same predicate body as the server's `declaredMultiValued`, so `multiselect` seeds an array without the `multiple` flag, as the engine stores it.
- One behaviour change beyond the card's named case, judged correct: a field whose served `defaultValue` is literally `null` used to seed `null` here and now seeds the marked option. That is what the server stores for it (`null == null` reaches the option fallback), so it is a convergence, not a drift.
- Observation, not a fault: the seed reads arity off `meta` (the object field), while the rendered widget's arity is `override.multiple ?? def.multiple` (a FormView override may differ). The server reads the object field alone, so the seed matches what omission would store; a view override that flips arity was already divergent from storage before this PR and is outside the card.

**Create-only gate versus ungated literal defaults — consistent with objectui#11914, and no path found where the public form refuses what the server would default. Right.**
- The server's `applyFieldDefaults` runs on the INSERT path only ("the UPDATE path never calls this"), so the option fallback is a create-time rule server-side as well. Gating the client seed on `!record` reproduces exactly that; an edit form with an unset column gets no option default from the server either, so leaving it empty is not a refusal of a server default. `/f/:slug` (`loadPublicForm`) always returns `record: null`, so on the public route the gate is always open and the card's measured case is covered.
- Literal defaults on this route being seeded even with a record (pre-existing, from #5727) is the asymmetry the dev flagged. It is out of the card and unchanged by this diff; the record value still overrides it via `hasOwnProperty`, so the only case it affects is an edit form over a column the row leaves unset, where it was already so before this PR.

**Reading the flag off `RenderableField.meta` — the same served data the server reads. Right.**
- `meta` is set to `objFields[override.field]`, the served object field whole ("at runtime it is the whole served object"); `normalizeOptions` only shapes the row's `options` to `{ value, label }` and discards `default`, which is why `options` cannot be the source. The server's `resolveOptionDefault(f)` reads `f.options[].default === true`, skips value-less marks, takes the first on a single-valued field and all on a multi-valued one; `optionListDefault` implements the same four rules on the same canonical key. Both read the object's field definitions; the card's own measurement (the internal New Case form preselects Low from the same served schema via `schemaDefaultValues`) confirms the served metadata carries the flag.
- A row built with no object field behind it has `meta` undefined and seeds nothing, which is the pre-PR behaviour.

### ② Semver level

- Diff publishes: one new runtime export and one new type export on `@object-ui/plugin-form`, plus a widened (more permissive) parameter type on a function that was not previously published. Additive public surface on a fixed-group package is `minor` under AGENTS.md's policy (no `major` in this repo; breaking changes also go as `minor` with the semantics in the body). The changeset `'@object-ui/plugin-form': minor` matches the diff. `Clause-②: yes` is correctly claimed: the PR widens a package entry.
- `apps/console`: the brief's premise that it is a private app does not hold on the tree — `apps/console/package.json` carries no `private: true` (the one private fixed-group member is `object-ui`, the VS Code extension), and `@object-ui/console` is a named member of the `fixed` group. Its `src/` changed, so `check-changeset-presence` owes a declaration; the policy ("declare once, not forced release") is satisfied by any added changeset, and the Changeset Declaration / Fixed Group / Bump Policy check-runs all concluded `success`. The fixed group bumps the console's version with plugin-form regardless. The repo's precedent for a user-visible console fix is to name it (e.g. `.changeset/11092-flow-label-reader.md` lists `'@object-ui/console': patch` beside the package line), so the console's own CHANGELOG would carry the entry; here the console fix is described only in the plugin-form entry's body. Not a gate failure and not a wrong level, but a `'@object-ui/console': patch` line is the repo-consistent shape and is recommended before merge.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none in the os-dev-report. Nothing to answer or escalate.
- Deviation 1 (option default gated to create while this route's literal defaults are not): answered in ① — consistent with #11914's "edit forms are never seeded" rule and with the server's insert-only `applyFieldDefaults`; the asymmetry is pre-existing and outside the card. No escalation.
- Deviation 2 (publishing the type `OptionListFieldLike`): answered in ① — required by objectui#7324 once `optionListDefault` is published; shape is minimal and type-only. No escalation.
- Out-of-scope finding (`normalizeOptions` drops `options[].default`, so the seed reads `meta`): confirmed on the source; reading `meta` is the correct source and no second defect follows from it. Noted, not filed, as the dev recorded.
- Gates declared to CI by the dev (whole `packages/plugin-form/` vitest run timed out locally; `apps/console/` not run locally; `check:spec-floors` no-artifact): the corresponding check-runs (Test shards, Type Check, Lint, Repo Gates, Build & E2E) are still in progress on this head and must conclude `success` before this verdict is acted on.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-13049-public-form-option-default`
Reviewed-by: `session_01XVp19E1MYUTFM3dnkwz8gB`

**VERDICT: PASS**
